Chinese game; played in Shanghai since at least the 1960s; may have originated there. Also known in Qingdao, Guangzhou. Spread to North America late 20th century.
40 cards: A(1) through 10 in each suit
Standard deck with face cards and jokers removed
Split deck equally; each player has a face-down stack.

items.text: Four Player Game: Deck divided equally; each player places one card face up. First three to slap the table are silent; fourth selects one. Selected player gives solution; if correct the fourth takes the four cards, otherwise the selected player takes them. Bluffing possible.

Card collection version: Two, three or four players. First correct solution takes the four cards under their stack. Players who run out can still call and win cards back. With three players, winner of previous set places two cards and others one each.

Multi-player dealer with scoring: Single shuffled stack; dealer drops four cards. First to find 24 scores a point. If no solution, first to call no solution scores one point; if someone then finds a solution the caller gets nothing and the finder scores two.

Extended operations and deck: Some allow powers and roots (e.g. 3^3=27), square root with a 2, or logarithms. Some include Jack=11, Queen=12, King=13 or Jokers 14 and 15. Factorials and approximations are not allowed; result must be exact.
